assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, deliver fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and are the clearest case of a new measurement method that changes what can be measured, from relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants to the prospective redefinition of the second. Experimentally concrete, with extremely well-characterised systematics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first Sr demonstration; Ye's group drove the record accuracy and the link to frequency combs and cold-atom many-body effects. The two-name credit is clean, though other lattice-clock groups (for example PTB, SYRTE, NIST/JILA Yb) and the single-ion clock lineage around Wineland and Hall/Haensch (already recognised in 2005 and 2012) bear on how the citation is worded.
assessment.maturity: Several independent labs worldwide reproduce 1e-18-level performance and clock comparisons agree; the interpretation is stable and the field is well past the proof-of-principle stage. Recognition is timely, and the redefinition of the second is still pending.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion citations.
Whether Ye's role should be weighed against other clock leaders such as NIST or PTB groups; I rely on memory of the priority dates and have not verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry underpins gravimeters, gradiometers, gyroscopes and tests of the equivalence principle and of the fine-structure constant. It is a precision-measurement tool in which matter-wave coherence is used as a sensor, which is precisely the kind of method-opening advance I value, and one whose field and commercial use have grown steadily.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard (first atom interferometers with gratings and light, Mach-Zehnder type), Bordé (the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer and theoretical framework) and Kasevich (light-pulse gravimetry and large-scale demonstrations with Chu) are the plausible trio. Chu's 1997 prize for laser cooling and the Kasevich-Chu work complicate who is credited for the interferometer itself; Keith Hinds, Ernst Rasel and others are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the lab (long-baseline and space-bound projects, field gravimeters) with a clear sensitivity record, though the headline applications to gravitational-wave detection and dark-matter searches remain prospective.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 1997 cooling prize and with Chu's own contributions.
Priority dispute between early demonstrations (1991 groups) and the theoretical framework.
Mixed state of fundamental-physics reach versus practical sensors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical readout and coherent control of single NV centres created a room-temperature solid-state qubit and nanoscale sensor for magnetic fields, electric fields and temperature, with reach into biology, materials science and quantum networks. The measurement capability is real, widely used and still expanding.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated single-NV optical detection of magnetic resonance and coherent control in 1997-2004; Lukin and collaborators opened the nanoscale sensing and quantum-register directions. Other leaders, such as Awschalom, Hanson and Yacoby, are not in the credited names, so a three-person split would leave a visible gap that the committee would have to defend.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is extensive across many labs and the techniques are routine tools. Quantum sensing applications are maturing, though the very largest impact (in vivo, industrial) is still developing.
uncertainties: Attribution is fragmented among many strong groups; Lukin's contribution is broad rather than the founding observation.
Overlap with the solid-state spin entry (B042) and with the 2025 and earlier quantum-information prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised controllable Hubbard models, the Mott-superfluid transition and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy, giving a new way to observe many-body quantum states. It is a measurement and control platform that has changed how correlated matter is studied.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner (with Bloch and Hänsch) observed the Mott transition and later built the quantum gas microscope; Bloch led the broader programme. Cirac and Dalibard contributed significantly as well, so a three-person limit forces a choice that I regard as the main difficulty of this candidate.
assessment.maturity: The Mott transition and microscopy results are replicated by many groups. The longer-term goal of solving open problems such as the Fermi-Hubbard phase diagram is not yet fully realised, but the platform is well established.
uncertainties: Which three of five credited names; Cirac and Dalibard are strong alternatives.
Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and with the 2022 and 2025 quantum-technology prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg-blockade interactions and optical-tweezer arrays have produced programmable arrays of hundreds of atoms for quantum simulation and gate-based computing, with high-fidelity gates and error-correction demonstrations. An experimentally striking development and a rapidly changing field.
assessment.attribution: Browaeys, Lukin and Saffman led the key blockade, entanglement and array-assembly experiments, and Zoller provided much of the theory (the Rydberg gate proposal with Jaksch and Lukin). Other array pioneers, for example Regal, Bernien and Endres, add to attribution difficulty, and Zoller is the natural fourth name that the three-person limit forces out.
assessment.maturity: Highly active, with strong independent confirmation across several groups, but the field is still moving quickly and the best long-term interpretation of its significance remains premature to fix.
uncertainties: Probably too recent for a prize if the field has not yet settled; the final form of the prize-worthy discovery is open.
Credit split across the tweezer-array, blockade and theory contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling between a superconducting qubit and a microwave resonator a standard method, giving dispersive readout and the basis of today's superconducting quantum processors. It is a clear experimental and conceptual advance with large downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal and the 2004 experiment; Wallraff and Schoelkopf carried the experimental programme. Girvin is the natural fourth name, and the three-person limit needs a choice. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits already honours part of this lineage, which I recall from outside the supplied materials and have not verified here.
assessment.maturity: Extremely well confirmed and in industrial use, so maturity is high; the timing question is rather one of fit after the 2025 recognition of superconducting circuits.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to honour a second superconducting-circuit prize so soon.
Allocation of credit between theory and experiment and the exclusion of Girvin.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ti:sapphire gain media and passive mode-locking (Kerr-lens and SESAM) made femtosecond lasers practical, compact and widely available, enabling frequency combs, ultrafast spectroscopy and attosecond science. An instrument-level invention with very broad impact, and exactly the kind of tool that opens new measurements.
assessment.attribution: Moulton demonstrated the Ti:sapphire laser, Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking, and Keller introduced the SESAM. The credit is plausible with three names, but the Kerr-lens work involved several co-authors (Spence, Kean) beyond the supplied names, and Hänsch, Hall, Krausz and Mourou/Strickland already hold related prizes.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and nearly universal use in labs. Timing is late rather than premature, with a risk that the field is seen as already covered by earlier ultrafast-optics prizes.
uncertainties: Priority and attribution for Kerr-lens mode-locking are not cleanly resolved from the supplied credit.
Overlap with the 2005 comb prize and the 2018 chirped-pulse and 2023 attosecond prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal and its experimental realisation in ion chains established trapped ions as a leading quantum-computing and simulation platform, with record gate fidelities and long coherence times. Strong, concrete experimental demonstration of coherent control.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller supplied the 1995 gate proposal; Blatt led a major experimental realisation, but the other leading experimental group (Wineland, already a laureate in 2012; also Monroe and others) is absent from the credit. That makes the fair configuration uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The platform is mature and independently confirmed by several groups. The part of the lineage that was already recognised in 2012 makes the remaining prize case narrower.
uncertainties: How much of this work is already covered by the 2012 prize for measuring and manipulating single quantum systems.
Overlap with B043 and B010, which share Cirac and Zoller.
